source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Acute mesenteric ischemia, especially given atrial fibrillation and severe abdominal pain that is disproportionate to early examination findings.","B":"Uncomplicated viral gastroenteritis, because nausea and vomiting make vascular causes of abdominal pain unlikely in this presentation.","C":"Mechanical low-back strain, because pain from the abdominal wall commonly produces severe symptoms despite minimal examination findings.","D":"Stable chronic peripheral vascular disease, because severe new abdominal pain is expected and does not require urgent vascular evaluation in this client."}}
source_row.rationale: Sudden, severe abdominal pain that is notably out of proportion to a relatively benign-appearing physical exam, particularly in a client with risk factors such as atrial fibrillation (embolic source) or vascular disease, is a classic warning sign of acute mesenteric ischemia, a vascular emergency requiring immediate evaluation given the significant risk of bowel necrosis if blood flow is not promptly restored.
source_row.source_detail: WSES 2022 AMI guideline Statements 1.1 and 1.5: severe pain out of proportion should be assumed AMI until disproven; CTA should be performed without delay; atrial fibrillation is an embolic risk source. World J Emerg Surg 2022;17:54, DOI 10.1186/s13017-022-00443-x; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
